Selected research & engineering work

Projects.

Four projects spanning drive diagnostics, energy recovery, power conversion, and thermal design. Each entry describes my role and the result reported in my CV.

01 / Ongoing
Modeling, simulation, and diagnostic algorithms
Supervisor: Bo Liu

Current-Based Fault Diagnosis for a PMSM Drive

I investigate six single-switch and fifteen double-switch inverter open-circuit configurations using MATLAB/Simulink, angle-domain current features, and a temporal convolutional classifier.

  • In one saved 66-record simulation study at 1000 rpm and 10 N·m, the validation-selected rule eventually identified all 63 fault records correctly, with no false locks on three normal records.
  • Timing remains an open problem: 2/18 single-switch cases met the half-cycle target and 42/45 double-switch cases met the three-quarter-cycle target. These results concern one operating condition and an inherited split with documented source overlap.
  • A separate sensor-gain prototype was replayed on 108 correlated perturbation cases derived from three normal parent records. This is exploratory evidence, not a validated final joint diagnostic model.

View code, model, results, and reproduction notes on GitHub ↗

My roleModeling, simulation, data processing, feature extraction, and algorithms

02 / Apr 2025 – Apr 2026
Core team member

EV Regenerative Braking and Energy Recovery

In a university innovation project, I co-authored a study of electro-hydraulic braking force allocation combining fuzzy control with improved particle swarm optimization.

  • The team tested the strategy through Simulink–CarSim co-simulation across UDDS, CLTC, and NEDC driving cycles. The published study reported final residual battery-charge increases of 1.45%, 3.15%, and 2.38%, respectively.
  • I contributed to a battery–supercapacitor hybrid storage architecture using a bidirectional Buck-Boost converter and compared SiC and Si-IGBT devices for switching losses and efficiency on a braking test platform.
  • The control-strategy results were published at IEEE EESPE 2026; I am the fourth author of five.

03 / Aug – Nov 2025
Utility model patent application

High-Gain Coupled-Inductor Buck-Boost Converter Circuit

I designed the PWM feedback-control and input EMI-filter circuits, connecting output-voltage sensing to duty-cycle adjustment for closed-loop regulation.

  • Specified an EMI network with four inductors and five capacitors, including differential- and common-mode inductors.
  • Used a two-resistor voltage divider for output sensing and an RC timing network for the PWM oscillator, with feedback compensation in the control circuit.
StatusUtility model patent application; grant not claimed
MethodsPWM control · EMI filtering · circuit design
04 / 2024 – 2025
Project leader

Air-Cooling Design for a Permanent-Magnet Wind Generator

I led the design of a fully enclosed cooling topology using rotor spokes to generate circulating airflow. The team built a coupled fluid–thermal–electromagnetic model using CFD/FVM and measured loss inputs.

  • Predicted a 73.2 K peak temperature rise near the central outlet and compared simulated temperatures with Pt100 measurements, obtaining a reported 5.92% simulation error.
  • Performed ventilation-duct sensitivity analysis and selected a 200 mm axial duct width.
  • The project reported 30% lower machine volume without additional energy consumption and an estimated cost reduction exceeding 50%.
My roleProject leadership, modeling, analysis
MethodsCFD/FVM · thermal analysis · measurement comparison
